text:
Anna P: noticing a few production alerts for high tail latency on dedicated pool eu-1. where's the best place to drill into per-pool latency + traces?

Raj K: start with the pool dashboard in Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pool-overview?var-pool=eu-1 — it has p50/p95/p99 and request rate by model.

Anna P: thanks. i can see p95 jump but need to know if it's batching / queueing or kernel/host-level. any specific panels to check?

Luis G: check these panels in that dash: "queue_depth", "active_workers", "gpu_utilization", and "kv_cache_hit_ratio". queue_depth -> if rising before p95 spike it's backpressure.

Emily T: also correlate with autoscale activity: dashboard has "scale_events" heatmap. if we had a spike + no scale because of cooldown, latency will climb.

Anna P: where are traces? want flame graphs or spans for a few slow requests.

Dan S: Honeycomb has traces. use this pre-filter: service:inference pool:eu-1 duration>2500ms and sample by trace_id. link: https://ui.honeycomb.io/redwood/datasets/inference/query?pool=eu-1&min_ms=2500 (internal)

metrics-bot: snapshot created by metrics-bot: https://snapshots.internal/abc123-pool-eu-1-1812345678 (contains p95 timeline + queue_depth) :robot_face:

Raj K: for quick PromQL checks, try:
```
avg_over_time(pool_latency_ms{pool="eu-1"}[5m])
quantile_over_time(0.95, pool_latency_ms{pool="eu-1"}[5m])
```
and queue depth:
```
sum(pool_pending_requests{pool="eu-1"}) by (pool)
```

Luis G: if you want kernel-level symptoms, check host metrics in node-exporter for that pool's node set: cpu steal, softirq, gpu memory pressure. i've seen softirq spikes correlate to tcp stalls.

Emily T: i dug into one trace earlier — issue looked like KV cache miss storms around certain prompt patterns. check kv_cache_hit_ratio drop at 14:12 UTC on 03/12.

Anna P: that aligns with the p95 spike window. should we tune alerting? current alert pool-high-latency triggers when p95 > 3000ms for 5m. for batch-heavy windows maybe we want 5m->3m window or increase threshold? thoughts?

Raj K: i'd prefer reducing noise: change to p95>3500ms for 5m for dedicated pools with known batchy workloads, but keep p99 at 8s for hard failures. open PR and let's review.

Dan S: opened PR #4567 with suggested alert change and added runbook link. pinging @Emily T and @Luis G for quick review.

Emily T: lgtm for threshold change, but add a note about when to rollback (if queue_depth stays high after scale).

Luis G: added comment to PR about correlating with kv cache misses and autoscale cooldown.

Anna P: perfect. one last ask — can someone attach the trace ids for the two slow requests i flagged? i'll post them in the incident doc.

Dan S: posted trace ids in the PR and incident doc: trace_id a1b2c3d4, e5f6g7h8. also added short Honeycomb query.

metrics-bot: alert "pool-high-latency-eu-1" resolved at 2026-03-12T15:20:00Z :white_check_mark:

Anna P: thanks all — i'll follow up in the incident doc with findings and next steps. :thumbsup:
